items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I guess he just offered me the chair in the orchestra... when he asked you to join his band

ctx.x: Well, I think the recordings belie such modesty. But, in any case, why don’t we move to another association after Fletcher Henderson, and that is Chick Webb.
Oh, yes. Dear, dear Chick Webb.
Do you recall the circumstances of joining that great orchestra?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] Let me see ... I'm trying to remember when if I was with Chick Webb's band. ... [INTERVIEWER] Were you at that time -- do you remember being with Chick Webb at that time? [INTERVIEWEE] No. At that time, I was with Fletcher Henderson.

ctx.x: I'd like to come now, you know -- we brought up your sax playing, your arranging, and your interest in the trumpet and your taking up the trumpet, which brings us to somewhere in 1928-29. Now let's go on to the band-leading and playing and other things that came up after that point. I'd like to get some notion -- is the next major thing that you do going to Fletcher Henderson's band, or is there something else that goes on before that?
Let me see ... I'm trying to remember when if I was with Chick Webb's band.
